name: RIGCHECK core loop (12 games)
description: The twelve games flagged coreLoop:true in data/catalogue/games.json. They are the fitting set the CPU/GPU split is calibrated against, so they are worth measuring on every machine even when nothing else is. Chosen for archetype spread, not popularity: 4 esports, 2 sim-cpu, 2 aaa-raster, 3 aaa-rt, 1 vram-heavy.
notes: The defaults are a NATIVE, NO-RT, NO-FRAME-GEN baseline. That is deliberate: it is the only pass that is comparable across every vendor and generation. Upscaled and RT passes are separate sessions, not a mixed run - the importer refuses to form a comparison edge across those axes anyway.

processName values are what PresentMon filters on. Verify each against Task Manager > Details on first run; the runner warns before capture when the named process is not running. A wrong name fails loudly (no frames captured), it does not corrupt a row.
Games without a built-in benchmark need a fixed, repeatable route. WRITE THE ROUTE DOWN and reuse it verbatim on every machine, or the numbers are not comparable between rigs.

games.name: Counter-Strike 2
games.scene: No official benchmark ships. Use a saved demo played back from a fixed tick (console: playdemo <name>, then let it run untouched - do not move the free camera), or the community FPS Benchmark workshop map. Whichever you pick, use the SAME one on every machine.
games.caution: Demo playback is not deterministic across game builds. Record the build in -GameBuild so a patch does not silently invalidate the comparison.

games.name: Dota 2
games.scene: Replay playback. Open a downloaded replay, seek to a fixed timestamp over a teamfight (a busy fight, not laning), park the camera and let it run at 1x speed.
games.caution: Seek to the same timestamp every time. A different fight is a different workload.

games.name: Rainbow Six Siege
games.scene: Options > Display > Benchmark. Start it, then confirm here as the first pass begins.
games.notes: The Vulkan build runs as RainbowSix_Vulkan.exe and the BattlEye-launched process may appear as RainbowSix_BE.exe. If the runner warns the process is not found, set processName to match what Task Manager shows and record the API you used.

games.name: Fortnite
games.scene: No benchmark mode. Use a saved replay with the camera locked to one player, or a fixed Creative island route. DX12 with Nanite/Lumen is the reference path; the DX11 Performance mode is a different renderer and must not be mixed into the same fixture set.
games.caution: Record which renderer (DX12 Lumen vs DX11 Performance) you used - they differ by multiples, not percentages.

games.name: Factorio
games.scene: Load a large fixed save, park the camera at a fixed position and zoom, and leave it running.
games.caution: READ THIS BEFORE CAPTURING. Factorio's render rate is bounded by its fixed 60 UPS update rate, so avg_fps here saturates at ~60 and measures almost nothing about the GPU. The figure that matters for this title is UPS from the headless command line (factorio.exe --benchmark <save> --benchmark-ticks 5000 --disable-audio), which PresentMon cannot see because that mode presents no frames. Capture this row only as a 'does it hold 60' check, and put the UPS figure in the source note by hand. Skipping this game is a legitimate choice.

games.name: Total War Warhammer III
games.scene: Options > Graphics > Run Benchmark, and choose the BATTLE benchmark. Confirm here once it starts.
games.caution: The battle benchmark is GPU-weighted and the campaign benchmark is CPU-weighted. They are NOT interchangeable. This suite standardises on battle; if you run campaign instead, say so in the source note or the row is not comparable.

games.name: Forza Horizon 5
games.scene: Settings > Video > Run Benchmark. It loops, so let it reach a steady loop before confirming here.
games.notes: One of the best-behaved fixtures in the suite: deterministic and very consistent frame pacing. If THIS one shows a high spread, the machine has background load - fix that before trusting anything else in the session.

games.name: Shadow of the Tomb Raider
games.scene: Graphics > Run Benchmark. Confirm here when the first scene starts.
games.notes: This benchmark reports CPU-bound and GPU-bound frame rates SEPARATELY on its results screen. Those two numbers are unusually valuable for fitting the CPU/GPU split - copy them into the source note by hand. RT shadows stay OFF for the raster reference row.

games.name: Cyberpunk 2077
games.scene: Settings > Graphics > Run Benchmark. Confirm here once the flythrough begins.
games.caution: RT off for this baseline pass. Cyberpunk's RT and path-tracing modes are enormously heavier loads and belong in a separate session with rtTier set accordingly - never merged into the raster rows.

games.name: Black Myth Wukong
games.scene: The standalone benchmark tool released separately from the game is the cleanest fixture here - run that if you have it. Otherwise use a fixed route in the opening area.
games.caution: The standalone benchmark tool is a DIFFERENT executable from the game. If you use it, set processName to whatever Task Manager shows for it, and record which one you used - the tool and the retail game are not necessarily the same workload.

games.name: Alan Wake 2
games.scene: No benchmark mode. Use a fixed outdoor route (the forest around Cauldron Lake is the usual choice: heavy foliage, worst case for this renderer). Walk the same 60 s route every time, starting from the same save.
games.caution: This is the mesh-shader gate title. On Pascal, Maxwell, GCN or RDNA 1 it will not launch at all - that is the expected WILL_NOT_RUN result, not a harness failure. Skip it on those cards; do not record a zero.

games.name: Hogwarts Legacy
games.scene: No benchmark mode. Hogsmeade is both the VRAM and the CPU worst case and is the only location worth using: stand at a fixed spot on the high street and walk a fixed 60 s loop from the same save.
games.caution: 1440p Ultra exceeds 8GB here. On an 8GB card expect texture streaming stutter that shows up in the 1% low, not the average - which is the point of measuring it. Do not 'fix' a high spread by lowering settings; record it.
